title: Tower of Hanoi example: moving six disks from A to C
summary: Starting with six disks stacked from smallest on top to largest at the bottom on rod A, move them all to rod C using rod B while preserving their order.
context: The Tower of Hanoi rules require moving only one disk at a time, taking it from the top of one rod and placing it onto the top of another, with smaller disks kept above larger disks at every step.
description: The upper half shows the starting state: three rods labeled A, B, and C from left to right, with six differently colored disks stacked from smallest at the top to largest at the bottom on rod A while rods B and C are empty.

The lower half shows the goal state: rods A and B are empty, and all six disks sit on rightmost rod C in their original order from smallest on top to largest at the bottom. A downward arrow in the middle labeled "Move all disks from A to C" summarizes the overall objective rather than implying the whole stack can be moved at once.

frames.title: Tower of Hanoi example: moving six disks from A to C
frames.explanation: This figure defines only the starting and goal states without expanding intermediate steps, which must be carried out as a sequence of legal single-disk moves.
